subject: Post-call recap + next steps: Healthlytics onboarding & benchmark recommendations
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Thorne <emily.thorne@healthlytics.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: Healthlytics onboarding & benchmark recommendations

Thanks again for the time this morning, Emily — good conversation and lots of alignment. Quick recap of what we discussed and a proposed plan so everyone is clear on next steps.

Scope (agreed):
- Run customer-specific evals on Redwood for two workloads: (1) clinical NER/extraction from discharge notes, (2) multi-label classification for readmission-risk categories.
- Work with your sample dataset (10k rows target for initial run; you mentioned we can start with ~2k to iterate).

Recommended initial models for benching (based on latency/cost/quality tradeoffs we discussed):
- redwood-llama2-13b-qa (4-bit) — fast, low-cost baseline for extraction with strong prompt-conditioning.
- redwood-mistral-70b-int8 — higher-capacity model for quality-sensitive cases (classification + tricky extractions).
- fallback: redwood-flan-t5-xxl for template-heavy classification prompts if we see hallucination patterns.

Eval format & scoring (proposal):
- Dataset: JSONL, each line = {"id": string, "input": string, "expected": string, "task": "ner"|"classification", "meta": {...} } (attached: redwood_eval_template.json)
- NER / Extraction metric: micro-F1 over canonical entity labels (normalize whitespace/casing; use token-level match after normalization). Target pass threshold = 0.82 (we can adjust based on initial run).
- Classification metric: accuracy and macro-F1 across labels. Target = 0.90 accuracy for MVP.

Prompt sets and temperature:
- We'll run each model with 3 prompt variants you provided + a zero-shot baseline; temperature 0.0 for extraction, 0.2 for classification experiments.

Security / data handling:
- You confirmed PII will be redacted before upload. For Private/Dedicated runs we can provide additional controls (VPC, dedicated GPUs) if you need audit-level separation.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Emily: share a 500-row redacted sample dataset by EOD Tue (I attached a sample CSV of prompts as an example).
2) Marcus (cc): allocate a short eval job; estimate token+time cost for 2k/10k examples and confirm model mapping.
3) Connor: prepare SOW draft and rough timeline.
4) Schedule 30-min handoff where Marcus + Lauren join to review dataset format and scoring details — propose Wed 3/22 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: healthlytics_sample_prompts.csv, redwood_eval_template.json

If that captures everything, I'll queue the SOW draft and follow up with calendar invites.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192

---

- Confirmed: dataset will be PII-redacted. We'll deliver a 500-row sample by Tue EOD and the full ~10k export (redacted) after the pilot SOW is signed.
- Scoring: we prefer token-normalized micro-F1 for NER and both accuracy + macro-F1 for classification — your proposed thresholds look reasonable as starting points.
- Timeline: can you include a quick estimate (ballpark) for Redwood hosted-run costs for 2k vs 10k examples per model and expected wall-clock runtime? That will feed into our procurement discussion.

Amit will be the technical owner on our side — adding him here. Amit, happy to set up the sample upload once we confirm the exact JSONL format Connor referenced.

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: Healthlytics onboarding & benchmark recommendations

Connor / Lauren / Emily — quick update from the engineering side after reviewing the sample and template. Plan below.

1) Runner + format
- We'll use Redwood Eval Runner (link: https://docs.redwood.ai/eval-runner#jsonl-format) with the JSONL template Connor attached. Each line: id, input, expected, task, meta (language, note_id).
- Scoring scripts: NER -> tokenized micro-F1 via our canonicalizer (whitespace/case/abbrev normalization). Classification -> exact-match + macro-F1. I'll push the scoring script to the shared drive and link it in the GH gist.

2) Model mapping & config
- redwood-llama2-13b-qa (4-bit) 
  - temp: 0.0 for extraction, batch size: 16 (continuous batching)
  - expected throughput: ~120 reqs/sec on a 1xA100-equivalent pod for short outputs
- redwood-mistral-70b-int8 
  - temp: 0.2 for classification, batch size: 8
  - use for the high-quality pass and for cases flagged by fallback rules

3) Thresholds (initial)
- NER: micro-F1 >= 0.82 = pass; 0.75–0.82 = investigate (prompt / template tuning); <0.75 = escalate to model change.
- Classification: accuracy >= 0.90 = pass; 0.85–0.90 = investigate.

4) Cost & runtime estimate (hosted) — ballpark for 2k / 10k examples (assumptions: avg input 600 tokens, avg completion 50 tokens, hosted token pricing per model approximated):
- redwood-llama2-13b-qa (4-bit):
  - 2k examples: ~3 GPU-hours total, hosted cost estimate: $420 (includes overhead).
  - 10k examples: ~15 GPU-hours, hosted cost estimate: $2,100.
- redwood-mistral-70b-int8:
  - 2k examples: ~6 GPU-hours, hosted cost estimate: $980.
  - 10k examples: ~30 GPU-hours, hosted cost estimate: $4,900.
Notes: Dedicated reserved capacity pricing will be different — I included GPU-hour estimates above if they want to compare. I'll refine numbers once we have the final dataset and exact token lengths.

5) Next steps & scheduling
- I'll provision the initial 2k job and run both models (three prompt variants + baseline) the week of 3/22.
- Proposed kickoff: Mon 3/22 10:00 AM PT — I'll share the runner config and scoring gist before the call.

Attachments: sow-draft-v1.docx (SOW with proposed timelines & acceptance criteria).

Emily — does that timeline work? If so, I'll spin up the job and share an embargoed results link so you can review before we circulate to procurement.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
